evals.prompt: Create a new production secret in AWS Secrets Manager following best practices.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Requests all required parameters upfront in a single prompt (`secret_name`, `secret_description`, `secret_type` [`database`, `api-key`, `oauth`, or `custom`], `aws_region`, and secure secret input handling without echoing plaintext secrets in logs/outputs) alongside optional defaults (`kms_key_id`, `enable_rotation=true`, `rotation_interval=30`, `recovery_window=30`, `allowed_principals`, `tags`)
Executes zero mutating KMS/Secrets Manager API calls before obtaining required parameters and user confirmation

evals.prompt: Write the dedicated Customer Managed KMS Key policy and `secretsmanager:CreateSecret` workflow for a `database` secret `prod/orders/aurora-pg` in `ap-south-1` (account `111122223333`) accessed by `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/orders-ecs-task-role`, explaining why `kms:ViaService` is critical.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Enables annual KMS key rotation (`enable-key-rotation`) and writes a KMS Key Policy preserving account root/key-admin access while scoping `kms:GenerateDataKey`, `kms:Decrypt`, and `kms:DescribeKey` with **`kms:ViaService: "secretsmanager.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com"`** (so principals cannot call `kms:Decrypt` directly bypassing Secrets Manager audit/IAM controls!)
Never logs or echoes plaintext secret values in outputs

evals.prompt: Show the recommended structured JSON secret schemas (using non-sensitive `<REDACTED>` placeholders — never real credentials!) for all four supported `secret_type` categories: `database`, `api-key`, `oauth`, and `custom`, and explain why standard keys (`engine`, `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `dbname`) matter for AWS Secrets Manager rotation.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Presents clean placeholder JSON schemas for all 4 types (`database` with standard AWS rotation keys `engine`, `host`, `port`, `username`, `password`, `dbname`; `api-key`; `oauth` with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `token_url`/scopes; and `custom`) with zero real secrets
Explains that AWS-managed and Lambda rotation templates expect the exact canonical `database` JSON field names (`username`, `password`, `engine`, `host`, `port`)

evals.prompt: We enabled 30-day automatic rotation on an RDS PostgreSQL secret in a private isolated VPC, and rotation immediately failed with `TimeoutError` inside the rotation Lambda! Explain the 4-step Secrets Manager rotation protocol (`createSecret`, `setSecret`, `testSecret`, `finishSecret`) AND every VPC/SG/IAM requirement for the rotation Lambda.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Details the 4-step rotation lifecycle (`createSecret` writes `AWSPENDING` -> `setSecret` updates DB user -> `testSecret` verifies login with `AWSPENDING` -> `finishSecret` moves `AWSCURRENT` label to the new version and `AWSPREVIOUS` to the old)

Diagnoses the private VPC `TimeoutError`: the VPC-attached rotation Lambda MUST reach **BOTH** the private RDS port (`5432` SG rule) **AND** the **`com.amazonaws.<region>.secretsmanager` Interface VPC Endpoint** (or NAT Gateway) over HTTPS `443`, plus `secretsmanager.amazonaws.com` `lambda:InvokeFunction` permission and KMS `Decrypt`+`GenerateDataKey`

evals.prompt: Author a least-privilege IAM Identity Policy + Secrets Manager Resource Policy (`put-resource-policy`) for `arn:aws:secretsmanager:ap-south-1:111122223333:secret:prod/payments/stripe-*` ensuring ONLY `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/payments-worker` can read `AWSCURRENT`, requiring TLS/HTTPS, and blocking wildcard secret enumeration.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Scopes `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` + `DescribeSecret` strictly to the exact secret ARN with `secretsmanager:VersionStage = AWSCURRENT` (and `kms:Decrypt` on the dedicated KMS key ARN), enforces `aws:SecureTransport: false` `Deny` (HTTPS-only), and avoids `secretsmanager:*` on `*`

evals.prompt: A developer wants to run `aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id prod/partner/oauth --force-delete-without-recovery` to clean up an old secret immediately! Explain Secrets Manager's recovery window (`7–30` days), mandatory tagging governance, and safe retirement checks before deletion.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill and warns strongly against `--force-delete-without-recovery` in production (permanent, unrecoverable immediate destruction if any service still reads it!)

Recommends checking CloudTrail `GetSecretValue` / `LastAccessedDate` (`DescribeSecret`) first, scheduling standard deletion with a **`30-day` recovery window (`--recovery-window-in-days 30`)** so `restore-secret` can recover immediately if an unknown consumer breaks, and applying lifecycle/ownership tags

evals.prompt: Check our caller identity and inspect `ap-south-1` in read-only mode (`secretsmanager:ListSecrets` metadata only — NEVER `GetSecretValue`!) to see if any secrets exist without automatic rotation or customer-managed KMS keys (`KmsKeyId`), and summarize best-practice remediation without mutating anything.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill and calls `sts:GetCallerIdentity` + metadata-only `secretsmanager:ListSecrets` in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands and zero `GetSecretValue` calls
Accurately reports live `ap-south-1` findings (cleanly reporting 0 secrets if none exist) and summarizes dedicated CMK + 30-day rotation + CloudTrail auditing checks
Makes zero mutating AWS calls

evals.prompt: Our CI rotation job has `secretsmanager:PutSecretValue` AND `kms:Decrypt` on the secret's dedicated KMS key, yet calling `PutSecretValue` fails with `AccessDeniedException: ... is not authorized to perform: kms:GenerateDataKey`! Explain why reading vs writing/rotating a CMK-encrypted secret requires different KMS actions.
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Identifies the root cause: while reading (`GetSecretValue`) uses `kms:Decrypt`, writing a new secret version (`PutSecretValue` / `CreateSecret` / `UpdateSecret`) generates a new KMS data key via envelope encryption and requires **`kms:GenerateDataKey`** (plus `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:DescribeKey` during rotation) on the Customer Managed KMS Key
Provides the concrete IAM policy and KMS key policy guidance granting `kms:GenerateDataKey` (scoped to the secret/CMK) for the rotation/writer role

evals.prompt: When our 12 ECS tasks cache a database connection pool and Secrets Manager rotates the single database user's password every 30 days (`SingleUser` strategy), active tasks briefly fail new connections with `password authentication failed` until their cache refreshes! How does Secrets Manager's **`AlternatingUsers` (two-user clone)** rotation strategy eliminate rotation downtime completely?
expectations: Activates the creating-secrets-using-best-practices skill

Contrasts `SingleUser` rotation (changes the active user's password in place) against **`AlternatingUsers` rotation** (maintains `userA` and `userB` with identical grants; rotates the **inactive** user's password in `AWSPENDING`, tests it, flips `AWSCURRENT` to the newly rotated user, while existing cached pools using `AWSPREVIOUS` continue working uninterrupted!)

evals.prompt: Query AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools to compare Secrets Manager **Managed Rotation for RDS (`ManageMasterUserPassword: true` / AWS-managed rotation without deploying a customer Lambda)** versus **Lambda-backed rotation (`RotateSecret` with `RotationLambdaARN`)**.
expectations: Queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`) with zero raw `aws` CLI commands

Contrasts **RDS-managed master user password rotation** (`ManageMasterUserPassword=true` — AWS manages the secret and rotates credentials natively without customer VPC rotation Lambdas!) against **Lambda-backed rotation** (required for non-master application DB users, `AlternatingUsers` strategy, OAuth/API keys, and custom targets)
